assumptions.label: ESTIMATE — assumptions editable; prototype metrics SIMULATED

fleet_size.note: Fleet size for fleet totals. The request can override it.

operating_hours_per_year.note: SMU (engine-on) hours incl. idle. Contractor excavators typically 1,000-2,000 h; quarries run more.

shift_engine_hours.note: Used only to express gains per shift.

idle_share_baseline.note: Komatsu: 38% average idle over ~75,000 North American machines; Volvo: 28-30% on ~450-machine fleets; ~20% cited as a realistic target.

production_m3_per_h.note: Fleet-average truck-loading output of a 20 t excavator (about 1.0-1.3 m3 bucket, about 20 s cycles, job efficiency applied).

cycle_time_s.note: Fleet-average truck-loading cycle. Used for the per-cycle-second unit value.

operator_wage_loaded_per_h.note: BLS median for construction equipment operators $28.66/h (May 2025) times an assumed ~1.4 burden (taxes, insurance, benefits). High = union metro rates.

machine_ownership_cost_per_h.note: Depreciation + interest + insurance. A new 20 t excavator at about $250-350k over 10,000-12,000 h. Cross-check against EquipmentWatch / USACE EP 1110-1-8 schedules in the pilot.

machine_operating_cost_ex_fuel_per_h.note: Maintenance, repairs, undercarriage, ground-engaging tools, lube. Excludes fuel.

fuel_working_l_per_h.note: Equipment World / Komatsu (snippet): 20 t fuel $8.55-20.25/h at $4.50/gal, i.e. about 7-17 L/h light to heavy. Dealer pages quote 15-30 L/h for 320 GC. Base is mid-duty.

fuel_price_per_l.note: EIA US on-highway diesel averaged about $3.66/gal in 2025 (= $0.97/L). Off-road dyed diesel is cheaper (low); many non-US markets are higher (high).

idle_fuel_l_per_h.note: Cat (snippet): most equipment burns about a gallon (3.8 L) an hour at idle. Dealers quote 3-5 L/h for excavators by size. Auto engine-speed control lowers the figure (low).

idle_hours_reduction_frac.unit: fraction of baseline idle hours eliminated
idle_hours_reduction_frac.note: Only avoidable idle is targeted; waiting-for-truck idle is context-gated and not coached. Going from the 35-38% average to the ~20% target would cut idle hours by ~45%, so base 15% is about a third of that. Cat engine idle shutdown already exists; Sentinel adds context and coaching.

idle_hour_smu_cost_per_h.note: Non-fuel cost of an idle hour: hour-based preventive maintenance, warranty hours used up while idling, lower residual value for higher-hour machines (qualitative in source). The $ figure is an assumption.

time_value_realization_frac.note: Share of ownership + labour cost of a freed productive hour that becomes real money (crew redeployed, job finished earlier, less overtime or rental). Variable costs (fuel, wear) are always counted in full.

billed_rate_per_h.note: Revenue proxy for the bid-risk term only. Web guides quote $150-250/h for a 20-30 t excavator with operator (unverified).

productivity_gap_frac.note: Fleet-average operator vs expert output gap. Secondary report of Caterpillar studies: operator skill alone gives a 10-15% spread in tons/h on the same machine. Novices are far worse (Volvo 80-operator study, forconstructionpros.com, page blocked) but the training lever covers them.

gap_closure_frac.unit: fraction of gap closed in year 1
gap_closure_frac.note: Share of the gap that coaching + targeted practice closes. No field evidence yet. This is the primary pilot KPI.

annual_operator_turnover_frac.note: Construction turnover is often quoted at 20-30%/yr (secondary, unverified). AGC 2025: 77% of firms find heavy-equipment operators hard to fill; 48% cite new hires who quit or fail to show.

time_to_proficiency_months.note: Time for a new operator to reach productive (not expert) output. BLS: apprenticeships run 3-4 years. Expert level is often quoted at 5-10 years.

novice_productivity_deficit_frac.note: Average output shortfall vs a proficient operator during the ramp-up.

time_to_proficiency_reduction_frac.note: Faster ramp from gap-targeted training. Kept equal to training_effect.time_to_proficiency_reduction_frac below: base = PBP meta-analysis -15% procedure time, high = Seymour 2002 RCT 29% faster, low = small effect. Simulator vendors claim up to 40% less machine time (VENDOR_CLAIM).

instructor_hours_per_new_operator.note: One-to-one instructor or mentor time per new operator.

instructor_cost_per_h.note: Loaded cost of an instructor or senior operator acting as mentor.

instructor_hours_reduction_frac.note: The Practice Analyser pre-screens each session so the instructor coaches only the flagged phases.

training_machine_hours_per_new_operator.note: Production machine taken out of work for training.

training_machine_hours_reduction_frac.note: Simulator vendor claim: up to 40% less real-equipment training time. High = that claim; base = well under it.

workers_exposed_per_machine.note: Operator + ground crew / spotter + truck drivers working around the machine.

recordable_rate_per_worker_year.note: BLS SOII 2023: construction had 2.3 recordable cases per 100 FTE (snippet).

machine_related_share_of_recordables.note: Share of recordables involving the machine (struck-by, caught-between, ingress/egress). Anchor: Liberty Mutual WSI Construction, struck-by = 12.2% of construction injury costs (snippet).

fatality_rate_per_worker_year.note: BLS CFOI 2023: construction fatal rate 9.6 per 100,000 FTE (1,075 deaths) (snippet).

machine_related_share_of_fatalities.note: NIOSH: 150 struck-by construction deaths in 2020, about 15% of about 1,000 construction deaths that year. Not all involve excavators (low).

cost_per_recordable_injury.note: NSC Injury Facts: $48,000 per medically consulted work injury (2024; $43,000 in 2023) (snippet). High adds uninsured indirect costs; OSHA puts indirect costs at 1.1-4.5x direct (https://www.osha.gov/safetypays/background).

cost_per_fatality.note: NSC economic cost per work death: $1.54M (2024), $1.46M (2023) (snippet). This is not a value of statistical life. High adds litigation and stoppage (assumption).

property_damage_incidents_per_machine_ye.note: Truck, structure or utility contacts. Bird (1969): 1 serious : 10 minor : 30 property-damage : 600 near-miss, so property-damage events outnumber injuries. The ratio is contested and used only as a sanity check.

high_risk_events_per_100h.note: Baseline precursor events (belt off while moving, person in zone, fast swing near truck). The demo rates are SIMULATED; the pilot measures the real baseline.

precursor_event_reduction_frac.note: Fewer precursor events after coaching + targeted training. Analogue only: proficiency-based simulation training cut excavation utility strikes 35-61% in a randomized study. Sentinel's Shift-2 reduction is SIMULATED.

precursor_risk_attribution_frac.note: Share of machine-related incident risk that runs through the observed precursor behaviours. Incident reduction = event reduction x attribution.

operator_sensitive_maintenance_share.note: Undercarriage, GET, hydraulic hoses and pins driven by technique. Trade press: operators drive undercarriage cost, which can be up to about 50% of tracked-machine maintenance (secondary).

wear_reduction_frac.note: Cat Operator Coaching ships 'Machine Health' tips, so Cat treats technique as a wear driver, but no public % was found. Weakest lever; excluded from the pitch headline.

truck_wait_hours_per_machine_year.note: Truck hours lost to excavator/truck mismatch or late task changes.

haul_truck_cost_per_h.note: Owned or rented articulated/on-road truck with driver.

truck_wait_reduction_frac.note: From calibrated P10/P50/P90 task-time and live remaining-time estimates.

bid_risk_reduction_frac_of_revenue.note: Smaller contingency or overrun from better duration estimates. Low = 0 (not cash until proven).

subscription_per_machine_per_year.note: Hypothetical Sentinel price (about $100/machine/month base). Not a Cat price.

one_off_per_machine.note: Install, integration and onboarding. Excludes proximity hardware (assumes Cat Detect-class hardware is already fitted).

co2_kg_per_l_diesel.note: EPA: 10,180 g CO2 per gallon of diesel = 2.69 kg/L (factor not re-fetched this session). Reported as a gain; not monetised.

practice_gap_closure_frac.note: Individual trainee closing part of their Practice Analyser gap to the Expert Motion Model.

expert_production_m3_per_h.note: Fallback expert output when a PracticeReport gives only cycle times.

time_to_proficiency_reduction_frac.unit: fraction of practice time to reach the proficient band

learning_rate_multiplier.unit: x skill gain per practice hour vs untargeted practice

error_reduction_frac.unit: fraction fewer critical errors vs conventional training

sources.claim: VR training to expert criterion: dissection 29% faster, 6x fewer errors (RCT, n=16)
Proficiency-based progression meta-analysis: -60% intra-op errors, -15% procedure time vs standard training
Technology-enhanced simulation vs no intervention: pooled effect ~1.1 SD on skills, 0.5 SD on patient outcomes
PBP training for utility excavation crews: -33% critical errors (RCT, n=12); utility strikes -35% to -61% after rollout
Excavator simulator-trained group matched the real-machine group after ~10 h on the real excavator (transfer)
Simulators cut real-equipment training time by up to 40%

training_effect.note: Base = the meta-analytic procedural-time gain (15%); high = the single-RCT figure (29%); low = small effect. Transfer from surgery to excavators is an assumption. Cohort results are SIMULATED.

estimate_base.label: ESTIMATE — assumptions editable; prototype metrics SIMULATED

productivity.basis: hours saved for the same work × (variable cost + realised ownership/labour)

idle_fuel.basis: avoided idle h × (idle fuel × price + non-fuel engine-hour cost)

training.basis: new operators/yr × (ramp deficit avoided + instructor h + machine seat h)

safety.basis: expected machine-related incident cost × precursor reduction × attribution (EXPECTED VALUE)

wear.basis: working h × non-fuel operating cost × operator-sensitive share × reduction

planning.basis: truck wait h avoided × truck cost + revenue × bid-risk reduction

uncertainty.method: 1000 Monte Carlo draws, triangular(low, base, high), independent, seed 7

sensitivity.name: gap_closure_frac
sensitivity.unit: fraction of gap closed in year 1

sensitivity.name: idle_hours_reduction_frac
sensitivity.unit: fraction of baseline idle hours eliminated

notes: Gains are modelled from editable assumptions; none is a measured customer result.
Prototype metrics are SIMULATED. Customer ROI needs a controlled pilot.
Safety is an expected value (probability × cost), not a promise.
low/high scenarios are all-conservative / all-optimistic stress corners; use the Monte Carlo P10–P90 in 'uncertainty' as the headline range.
